headline: Samsung Electronics is forecast to post its first quarterly operating profit above 100 trillion won, driven by memory chips.
score_reason: Forecast from broker estimates rather than a reported result; kept at the pool level.
importance_line: The profit would show how much the AI-driven memory shortage is paying chipmakers and shape memory prices for PC and phone buyers, but it is an estimate until Samsung reports on Thursday and its chip-contract and device units are losing money.
summary: The Korea Herald reports that brokerage estimates compiled by FnGuide point to a Samsung third-quarter operating profit of about 108.1 trillion won ($80.2 billion), nearly nine times a year earlier, which would be its first quarter above 100 trillion won. The jump is attributed to memory chips, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the fast memory stacked beside AI processors, while its contract chipmaking unit is expected to stay loss-making; Samsung publishes preliminary figures on Thursday.
notes: Analyst forecast, hedged as such in the entry.
